380YE Summer Solstice Imperial elections.d: New senators included Oria for Feroz, Brother Ibrahim the South Paw for Bastion, Alessandra Serafini for Sarvos, Irena Arkady for Karov, Tanwyn Ankarien for Spiral and Edmundo of Endsmeet for Zenith. Aureliana Perpetua Nicasia Saverio di Sarvos became Imperial Consul and Zanferr i Ezmara i Erigo Imperial Fleet Master. New generals were Zoran Orzel, Sullik and Dietrich Nieschteri Rezia von Temeschwar. In the Synod, Levitia of Endsmeet became Cardinal of Courage and Ephron of Adina's Charge Imperial Inquisitor. Barthol de Rondell became Warmage and Finn Finnsson Imperial Seer. White granite went to holders including Meric Freysson (406T), and Azazel of Ravensfell took the Great Forest weirwood on a reduced term.

n.Dawn: Weirwater kept its incumbent senator, Zoran Orzel took command of the Golden Sun, Isabella de Rondell was appointed Healer of Dawn, and Abaddon De Rondell and Lady Eleanor de Rondell retained their Synod posts.
n.Highguard: Brother Ibrahim the South Paw became senator for Bastion, the Granite Pillar's general was returned, Sariel kept the post of Virtue Inquisitor of Wisdom and Ephron of Adina's Charge was elected Imperial Inquisitor.
n.Imperial Orcs: The incumbent general of the Summer Storm was returned to the Military Council.
n.Navarr: Miaren returned its incumbent senator, the Black Thorns kept their general, and Wyl Brackensong became Broker of Treji Wayhouse.
n.The Brass Coast: Oria became senator for Feroz, while the Red Wind Corsairs' general and the Mistress of the Glass Parador were returned.
n.The League: Alessandra Serafini became senator for Sarvos, Dietrich Nieschteri Rezia von Temeschwar took the Towerjacks, and Jan Von Schmied De Temeschwar became Northbound Trademaster.
n.The Marches: Mitwold kept its senator, the Drakes and the Tusks kept their generals, and Thomas Astwich became Sheriff of Overton.
n.Urizen: Tanwyn Ankarien and Edmundo of Endsmeet won Spiral and Zenith while Redoubt kept its senator; Levitia of Endsmeet became Cardinal of Courage and Juliana of Phoenix Reach Civilian Commissioner of Urizen.
n.Varushka: Irena Arkady became senator for Karov and Sullik took command of the Army of the Northern Eagle.
n.Wintermark: Sermersuaq kept its senator, the Fist of the Mountain its general, Jorma Steelhail and Girthwynn Frythsdottir Tokling kept their Gatekeeper posts, and Thanmir Whiteraven became Civilian Commissioner of Wintermark.

t.Miaren: The incumbent senator for Miaren was returned at the Summer Solstice.

380YE Summer Solstice winds of fortune.d: The red star grew, the Phoenix faded, and stars went out over Skarsind, Holberg, Bregasland, Segura and Necropolis. Curses struck Astolat, Tassato, Casinea and Redoubt. The Black Thorns fought for Liathaven. A decision was needed on where to inter Empress Giselle, whose body was saved from Grendel looters in Sarvos. The Wintermark Hallow of the Green World touched all nations, especially Holberg. Reikos saw Llofir's transformations, Yael's arrival and a possible miracle. The Marches' Spring planting failed. Nazares and a spreading sorrow threatened Zenith. The Icy Crag college was completed in Miekarova. Fog lingered on the Bay of Catazar, and veils faded over Madruga and Zenith but not Tassato.

n.Dawn: Inhabitants of Astolat, particularly those with military units, were warned that curses were affecting the territory.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: their earlier sneak attack on Sarvos, during which they robbed Empress Giselle's tomb, is recalled.
n.Highguard: Highguard faced Llofir's transformations, Yael's arrival and a possible miracle in Reikos, a curse on Casinea's farmers, stars going out over Necropolis, and a say in where Empress Giselle would be laid to rest.
n.Imperial Orcs: The stars began going out over Skarsind, one of the worrying celestial phenomena of the season.
n.Jotun: The Black Thorns were fighting to reclaim Liathaven from Jotun control.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns' presence in Liathaven, fighting to retake it from the Jotun, was said to offer opportunities for the Navarr.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast saw stars going out over Segura, an Asavean temple invitation tied to Nemoria, lingering fog on the northern Bay of Catazar, and the veil over Madruga fading away.
n.The League: A League citizen, Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, was to be crowned Empress, while the League also dealt with Giselle's tomb, stars dimming and the Green World over Holberg, and a curse and persisting veil over Tassato.
n.The Marches: After the failed Autumn harvest and defeat in the Mournwold, the Spring planting also failed, bringing curses and opportunities, while stars went out over Bregasland.
n.Urizen: Zenith was threatened by Nazares's binding of Winter spirits into the dead and a spreading sorrow, Redoubt suffered a curse, and the veil over Zenith faded.
n.Varushka: Varushka was tagged in the omens of the red star, and the Summer college of the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun was completed near Volchitrava in Miekarova.
n.Wintermark: The Sherard Hunters of Wintermark raised the Hallow of the Green World, whose touch was felt across all ten nations.

t.Astolat: Astolat fell under curses, with military unit owners especially affected.
t.Bay of Catazar: The eerie fog over the northern waters of the bay persisted.
t.Bregasland: The stars began going out over Bregasland amid the Marches' failed harvests.
t.Casinea: Casinea suffered curses, with farmers particularly affected.
t.Holberg: Stars began going out over Holberg, the Hallow of the Green World had a particularly profound effect there, and its Empress Lisabetta von Holberg awaited coronation.
t.Liathaven: The Black Thorns were fighting in Liathaven to reclaim it from the Jotun.
t.Madruga: The strange shroud over Madruga's night skies faded and disappeared shortly before the Solstice.
t.Miekarova: The Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, a Summer college near Volchitrava under Cathan Canae's patronage, was completed and began recruiting.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the defeat in the Mournwold is cited as one of the Marches' recent woes.
t.Necropolis: The stars began going out over Necropolis.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt suffered curses, especially affecting castle owners, and its publishing house the Spider's Vantage Spire issued Livia Cascade's accounts of past-life visions.
t.Reikos: Reikos was transformed by the eternal Llofir, saw Yael and Brother Jared counter Golan's teachings amid a possible miracle, and needed Synod decisions on its esoteric plants and fungi.
t.Sarvos: The fog over Sarvos was seared away by Day magic, and the fate of Empress Giselle's body, saved from the Grendel raid on the Alivetti estates, awaited decision.
t.Segura: The stars began going out over Segura.
t.Skarsind: The stars began going out over Skarsind.
t.Tassato: Tassato suffered curses, especially affecting magicians, and the Penumbral Veil over its skies persisted.
t.Zenith: Nazares was binding Winter spirits into the newly dead and a pall of sorrow spread from a ruined spire, though the veil over Zenith faded.

r.Miekarova/Srodkoja: Mentioned in passing: Srodkoja is not named; the page only places the new Icy Crag college near Volchitrava in Miekarova.

380YE Summer Solstice winds of war.d: Dawnish and Varushkan armies cleared Dawnguard but made only slight inroads into the Carmine Fields. In Sarvos, under a new magical fog, citizens rose against the Grendel, who withdrew with their plunder before the Imperial armies arrived. Iron Confederacy slave mercenaries hired by the military council nearly sparked an incident, then left. In Spiral the Grendel narrowly held Ossuary, and Apulus sank into the sea. The Jotun came within a whisker of taking Serra Briante. In the Mournwold they retook Freemoor and Ore Hills, with its new fort, and half of Greensward. Elsewhere Llofir's servants overran Tamarbode, the Jotun stalled in Kallavesa, an undead host marched from Karsk through Weirwater, and the Hierro left Segura.

n.Dawn: The Golden Sun and the reborn Gryphon's Pride freed Dawnguard, while the Hounds of Glory helped secure Sarvos and the Eastern Sky and Green Shield fought in Spiral. An undead host is now heading for Semmerholm.
n.Druj: The Barrens orcs lost all their recent gains in Dawnguard despite Spring and Night magical defences, but held the Carmine Fields fiercely, especially under the Black Wind banner.
n.Grendel: The Grendel abandoned Sarvos and Uccelini with their plunder after the uprising and lost several ships. In Spiral they clung to Ossuary with reinforcements from the south-east, but lost Apulus and its unfinished fortifications to the sea.
n.Highguard: The Citadel Guard drove on Ossuary and the Granite Pillar held the Necropolis coast, while Highborn armies helped defend Kahraman. In Reikos, Highborn ruins and heritage were being unmade by the servants of Llofir.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Winter Sun harried the Jotun in Kahraman. The Summer Storm fought at the Battle of Ore Hills, where its orcs were seized by the voice of the Jotun ancestor Sjöfn of the Bittenblade. The few Hierro left in Segura asked to join the Imperial Orcs.
n.Jotun: The Jotun almost conquered Serra Briante and retook the Mournwold gains, Ore Hills fort included, while also taking half of Greensward. They advanced slowly into Kallavesa but were losing southern Liathaven to the Black Thorns.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns slipped through Kahraman into Liathaven with warbands from across Navarr and began retaking Beacon Point, as survivors flocked to their standard. The Quiet Step fought in Freemoor and gave warning of the Jotun march on Greensward.
n.The Brass Coast: The Red Wind Corsairs raided Jotun baggage trains in Kahraman, where magic brought fertility along the Scorrero, and the Freeborn Storm sailed for Sarvos. The Hierro orcs left Segura for Jotun lands.
n.The League: Urged on by the Mayor of Caricomare and the League Assembly, the citizens of Sarvos rose against the Grendel and saved their city from fire. They suffered heavy losses and the theft of much of their wealth.
n.The Marches: The Tusks held against the Howling Night in Kahraman, and the Bounders and Drakes fought in the Mournwold, where Ore Hills, Freemoor and half of Greensward were lost. Orchard's Watch and the Singing Caves held; Marchers say Jonah Gold warned the miners.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the dead rising in Karsk were casualties of the recent war with the Thule, and messages were exchanged between the Thule and the Varushkans.
n.Urizen: Urizen magic, including the Winter's Ghosts curse, harried Spiral. Any Urizen children held hostage at Apulus are believed lost when the town sank.
n.Varushka: The Golden Axe fought in the Barrens, and the Coven of the Indomitable Sun's ice castle helped save Serra Briante. Ushkans joined the Black Thorns, while thousands of the dead rose in Karsk and marched into the Semmerlak.
n.Wintermark: Winterfolk faced the strongest Jotun in Kahraman and exchanged their dead with them. Wintermark magic slowed the Jotun advance into Kallavesa and roused the forests of Highrod.

t.Bay of Catazar: A new magical fog drifted down over the northern Bay. The fleeing Grendel vanished into it, while the Freeborn Storm sailed through it without meeting the enemy navy.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: warbands from Brocéliande joined the Black Thorns on their march into Liathaven.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: warbands from Hercynia joined the Black Thorns on their march into Liathaven.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks relished fighting beside the warriors who had helped liberate Holberg from the Druj.
t.Kahraman: Around forty thousand Jotun pushed back the Imperial defenders, and four thousand fell. Serra Briante was left on a knife edge, saved only by an enchanted ice fortress.
t.Kallavesa: The Jotun slowly spread across the Westmarsh offering the Choice, but Night and Spring enchantments meant they made no headway in conquering it.
t.Karsk: Several thousand human and orc dead from the war with the Thule rose, gathered near the Dark Heart, and marched into the Semmerlak.
t.Liathaven: Some seven thousand Navarr under the Black Thorns raised their standard and began a merciless guerrilla campaign to free the south, while survivors rallied to them.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the Freeborn Storm sought payback for the Grendel attack on the Madruga shipyards, and the fleeing Grendel did not sail towards Madruga.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: warbands from Miaren joined the Black Thorns on their march into Liathaven.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: two bands of Ushkans from Miekarova marched with the Black Thorns.
t.Mournwold: Eight thousand fell as the Jotun retook all the land the Empire had liberated and seized half of Greensward. Orchard's Watch and the Singing Caves held.
t.Necropolis: The Granite Pillar took defensive positions along the fog-shrouded coast with Wintermark's magical support, but saw no Grendel; the situation was unchanged.
t.Reikos: A wellspring of Spring magic from the Sign of Tamar brought Llofir's children across Reikos, unmaking ruins and restoring forest. Tamarbode was effectively conquered by them.
t.Reinos: The Hierro clan marched out of Segura into the red hills of Reinos to face the Choice of the Jotun.
t.Sarvos: A citizen uprising under magical fog drove out the Grendel, and the city was again unequivocally Imperial. It was left fire-scarred and stripped of much of its wealth, with little recovered.
t.Segura: The Hierro clan broke camp near Anduz and left peacefully for Jotun lands, their chieftain thanking the Freeborn. The few who stayed asked to join the Imperial Orcs.
t.Semmerholm: The undead host marching through Weirwater was expected to enter Semmerholm near the Semmerstones less than a week after the Solstice if it did not turn aside.
t.Spiral: Imperial armies made gains in Ossuary but no region changed hands; the Grendel kept the territory, only just. Spiral was wracked by curses, storms and the sinking of Apulus.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the mithril miners and wagon-drivers of the Singing Caves carry their bounty to Tassato.
t.The Barrens: Imperial armies recaptured Dawnguard and set up outposts on the northern edge of the Carmine Fields, which stayed firmly in orc hands amid red rivers and festering wounds.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: warbands from Therunin joined the Black Thorns on their march into Liathaven.
t.Weirwater: An army-sized host of the walking dead emerged north of Culwich and marched south-west, overwhelming a garrison that tried to stop it and damaging villages and roads.

r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: The Jotun besieged the frozen citadel near the Great Mine of Briante and came within a whisker of conquest, but the region stayed in Imperial hands.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: Held by the Jotun, who were supported by a tower of ice and iron over the ruins of Damata; the Navarr gave the region a wide berth on their way north.
r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: Night magic swallowed Kallavesa Marsh in mists, sheltering those fleeing the Jotun and hiding those resisting them.
r.Kallavesa/Skymark: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun were forging routes towards Skymark.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: The Jotun spread cautiously across the West Marsh offering the Choice, but enchanted mists and disease meant they made no headway in conquering it.
r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: Jotun scouts were sighted, but the Sherard Hunters woke the trees to entrap them and aid the defenders.
r.Liathaven/Beacon Point: The Black Thorns rallied here and made significant headway; if nothing changes they will claim the region by the end of next season.
r.Liathaven/Western Scout: Messengers were sent to seek resistance groups here; if nothing changes, Western Scout should be liberated by the end of the year.
r.Mournwold/Freemoor: The Jotun drove the Empire out village by village, aided by Knights of the Crimson Fields, and retook all of Freemoor.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: The Tower of the North and the Corazón attacked, taking nearly half the region and damaging Orchard's Watch. Overton and the Singing Caves held.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: The Ore Hills were lost after a great battle, and the almost-finished Imperial fort fell to the Jotun, who call it 'The Tribute'.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Part of the Quiet Step raided Jotun supply trains in Southmoor and discovered the march on Greensward. The Jotun already hold a fortification here.
r.Necropolis/Highrod: The Sherard Hunters roused Highrod's forests around the ruins of the First Sentinel, which the Granite Pillar used as a base.
r.Reikos/Chalcis Mount: The Spring magic finally swirled across the ruined walls of High Chalcis and the Chalcis Mount.
r.Reikos/Grey Charge: The wellspring of Spring magic and the children of Llofir spread quickly through Grey Charge.
r.Reikos/Haros Water: The magic reached Haros Water and the ruins of Haros, bringing rot and regrowth.
r.Reikos/Longshire: The wave of Spring magic washed over Longshire, consuming ruins and renewing growth.
r.Reikos/Riverwatch: The wave of Spring magic washed over Riverwatch and eddied around the walls of Tabernacle.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: The magic poured out from the Sign of Tamar, and Llofir's forces effectively conquered Tamarbode; the fate of the orcs left there is unclear.
r.Sarvos/Bocche: The new magical fog spread across Bocche during the uprising.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: Citizens rose against the Grendel in the city, saving it from fire before the Grendel withdrew by sea. A cleared site showed no sign of fortification work.
r.Sarvos/Foracci: The magical fog spread along the swollen Gancio to Foracci.
r.Sarvos/Riposi: The magical fog spread across southern Riposi.
r.Sarvos/Uccelini: Fog cloaked Uccelini, and the Grendel there also departed into the mists.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Potent Night magic and storms turned the coast into quicksand and sank the port and Grendel fortifications, killing many orc civilians and captives.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: The Empire drove hard on Ossuary and made gains, but the reinforced Grendel narrowly held it.
r.Spiral/Screed: A tempest of crimson lightning engulfed Screed around the Black Plateau, which Imperial troops avoided.
r.Weirwater/Garthmoor: As the Solstice dawned, the undead host was believed to be crossing Garthmoor towards Applefell.

A banner of Thorns.d: With the Black Thorns fighting alone in southern Liathaven, the wind offered four opportunities. The Senate could enlarge the army using arriving volunteers. A Synod statement could grant supporting warbands a bonus if both the Black Thorns and the Quiet Step attacked in Liathaven. Navarr generals could issue the ruthless 'An Enduring Example' order. A strike on a gate could open the hidden Paths of Lan Thúven through the vallorn. At the Summer Solstice the Navarr liberated the Paths. Corey Brackensong led the Navarr Assembly's call for unity, but the two armies fought in different territories. The Senate began the two-season enlargement, with 50 mithril and 10 thrones still owed. General Ulric Y'Basden ordered the Black Thorns to become the dark beneath the trees.

n.Jotun: The Jotun, who had purged the Navarr of Liathaven, faced a growing resistance. They lost control of the Lan Thúven gates and suffered General Ulric Y'Basden's merciless 'Enduring Example' campaign, though fleeing warriors reinforced Jotun armies beyond Liathaven.
n.Navarr: The Navarr rallied to the Black Thorns and seized the Paths of Lan Thúven, giving their armies passage across the vallorn. The Senate began enlarging the Black Thorns, and the National Assembly issued a call for unity to retake Liathaven.

t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: Hordalant, to the west, was noted as holding unknown numbers of orcs who might strike at the Black Thorns.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman was noted as hosting major Jotun forces to the east that might be sent against the Black Thorns.
t.Liathaven: Liathaven was the focus of the Navarr liberation campaign. The Black Thorns fought ruthlessly in the south, began their enlargement there, and gained the hidden Paths of Lan Thúven linking the territory's north and south across the vallorn.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step was fighting in the Mournwold, which was noted as holding major Jotun forces, while many Navarr urged that army to turn to Liathaven instead.

r.Liathaven/Liath's Ring: Mentioned in passing: there was no news from Liath's Ring in northern Liathaven.
r.Liathaven/Liaven's Glen: Mentioned in passing: there was no news from Liaven's Glen in northern Liathaven.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: West Ranging holds the northern Gate of Lan Thúven near the destroyed Silent Stand steading, once guarded by a Jotun warband. With the Paths liberated, Navarr armies could treat it as adjacent to Western Scout.
r.Liathaven/Western Scout: Western Scout, on the edge of the vallorn, holds the southern Gate of Lan Thúven by the ruins of Hidden Walk steading, once guarded by an isolated Jotun warband. It became the southern end of the Navarr route through the vallorn.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: Mentioned in passing: the Hidden Walk Navarr once used the hidden path to travel deep into the Westwood.

A question of provenance.d: As Spring magic transformed Reikos, eerie fungi spread through vinum, grain and produce. They spoiled crops but proved tasty and nourishing, and their mulch helped herb gardens. The Synod could issue an exclusionist judgement, boosting congregations but reducing production, or an inclusionist one, increasing production and sending curious materials to the congregations. Magisters also warned that such widespread effects should not have been possible without a Declaration of amity for Llofir, and urged the Conclave to investigate. With Highborn Assembly support, Gravus of the Shattered Tower carried an exclusionist message into Reikos. The congregations there were reinforced while businesses, farms, forests and herb gardens lost output. The Conclave also stripped the herald Gilean of her amity.

n.Highguard: The Highborn of Reikos were guided by their own Assembly to shun Llofir's influence in the name of Vigilance, renewing their attendance at congregation but destroying suspect goods and losing production across their businesses, farms, forests and herb gardens.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard of Urizen moved to Reikos after the Solstice to try to capture Tamarbode from Llofir's forces.

t.Reikos: Weird Spring-born fungi spread across the territory, and after the exclusionist judgement its congregations gained votes and liao while its businesses, farms, forests and herb gardens produced less as people discarded suspect materials.

r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Mentioned in passing: Tamarbode was named as the region the Citadel Guard of Urizen sought to capture from the forces of Llofir.

A season of mushrooms.d: Fungus, mould and ivy consumed corpses, ruins, timber and roads, erasing the Druj's poisons but also centuries of Highborn history. Chapters fought daily to save prized buildings, helped by Lucifer Son of Cyrus's auras of Courage and by a dozen captains supporting a great ossuary. Together with Llofir's power they located and destroyed many Druj miasma pillars, reducing the survivors to small zones of terror. A dark new forest engulfed the Sign of Tamar in Tamarbode, guarded by myconoid soldiers, and its Druj camps vanished. By the Autumn Equinox the magic had faded, leaving Reikos verdant and possibly better able to support a fourth Highborn army.

n.Druj: Their foul legacy in Reikos was washed away and many of their miasma pillars were destroyed, while the Druj remnant camps in Tamarbode disappeared without trace once the new forest appeared.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Sister Hepzibah's voice is said to have cut through battlefields from Karsk to Spiral, the latter a Grendel-held territory.
n.Highguard: The Highborn of Reikos saw the Druj taint erased but lost much of their centuries-old legacy, labouring daily to save their chapter houses, while Highborn captains and Lucifer Son of Cyrus helped destroy Druj miasma pillars.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Skywise Kray of the Imperial Orcs is named among the captains who brought retinues to Reikos to support the great ossuary.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: some speculate the force in Tamarbode crept out of Brocéliande, and the apothecaries of Peakedge Song are noted as interested in new medicinal plants.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Karsk is named as one of the battlefields where Sister Hepzibah once fought.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: some suggest the thing that seized Tamarbode may have snuck out of Brocéliande to the north-west.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: named in a vignette as one of the battlefields where Sister Hepzibah's voice was heard.
t.Reikos: The territory was transformed in a single season from a Druj-blighted ruin into wild meadow, forest and marsh, losing most of its ruins and much Highborn history while its villages, towns and key resources were kept clear.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: named in a vignette as one of the battlefields where Sister Hepzibah's voice was heard.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the apothecaries of Peakedge Song are said to be keen to see what new medicinal plants the magic reveals.

r.Reikos/Broken Ride: The existing opportunity to build a fortification here became of even greater interest to the Vigilant, as it would also allow watch over events in Tamarbode.
r.Reikos/Grey Charge: Mentioned in passing: Imperial forces destroyed several orc camps in Tamarbode during the earlier cleansing of Grey Charge.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Something unknown seized the region, raising a dense dark forest around the Sign of Tamar patrolled by myconoid soldiers who turn back armed intruders, and the Druj camps there vanished.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: Mentioned in passing: the region is not directly discussed; the page's great ossuary is a project in Reikos, and Spiral is named only in a vignette.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: Mentioned in passing: its apothecaries are keen to see what new medicinal plants the Spring magic and Druj domination might reveal for the Garden of High Chalcis.

Allocate Legacy.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Spiral and seconded by the senator for Sermersuaq. It allocated the Legacy bourse seat, located in the Ossuary region of Spiral, as a national bourse position. The motion passed. The Legacy therefore became a national position, due for its first appointment at the Autumn Equinox 380YE.

n.Grendel: With Grendel holding Spiral at the time, it was Spiral's senator who proposed making the Legacy a national bourse position, with appointment due at the Autumn Equinox 380YE.

t.Spiral: Spiral's senator proposed the motion, which turned the Legacy, a bourse seat within the territory, into a national position.

r.Spiral/Ossuary: The Legacy bourse seat in Ossuary was allocated as a national position and was due for appointment at the Autumn Equinox 380YE.

Archive:380YE Summer Solstice Imperial t.d: The list named each territory's senator, the Senate's appointed posts, commissioners and sinecures, every general of the Military Council, the cardinals, gatekeepers and virtue inquisitors of the Synod, the archmagi and grandmasters of the Conclave, and the holders of Imperial and national Bourse seats. Several sinecures, including the Dean of Pilgrims and Keeper of Aurelie's Garden, stood vacant, as did the Urizen Legacy. Senator Dušan of Miekarova had been revoked by the Synod but re-elected, and could not be revoked again before his next normal election. The Damatian Cliffs remained held by the Jotun and the Stonefield Ice Caves by the Thule. The Great Pits of Ennerlund were being repaired and were expected to produce mithril shortly after the solstice.

n.Dawn: Dawn held three Senate seats, four generals including Tancred de Rondell of the Hounds of Glory, and the Courage virtue inquisitor's post, with Ozren de Orzel and Agnetha De Rondell serving as cardinals of Pride and Wisdom.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named; Spiral, which it held, still appeared on the roll with Tanwyn Ankarien listed among the senators of Urizen.
n.Highguard: Highguard held four Senate seats and three generals, with Jared as Cardinal of Loyalty and Highguard citizens filling Synod posts such as Imperial Inquisitor, Auditor of Senatorial Accountability and Custodian of the Imperial War Memorial.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs held one Senate seat through Irontide Vio of Skarsind, two generals, Atla as Cardinal of the Way, and the Steel Fist and Brilliant Shore Bourse seats.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Damatian Cliffs Bourse seat was recorded as held by the Jotun.
n.Navarr: Navarr held three Senate seats and two generals, with Hywel Summercrow as Chaplain Consular and Idris Eternal holding the Thimble.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast held four Senate seats and three military commands, including Admiral Edgardo i Ruiloba i Guerra of the Freeborn Storm, as well as the Broken Shore Bounty Bourse seat.
n.The League: The League provided the Empress, Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, along with four senators, two generals and the cardinals of Ambition and Vigilance, and it held the Regario Dossier and the Master of the Imperial Mint.
n.The Marches: The Marches held three Senate seats and four generals, with Henry Ward as civilian commissioner and Robert Shanks operating Brock's Toll.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Stonefield Ice Caves, a Wintermark Bourse seat, were recorded as held by the Thule.
n.Urizen: Urizen held three Senate seats and was listed as also seating Spiral's senator; it had one general, Nicassia Avicia of the Citadel Guard, while Maximillian served as Conscience of the Senate and Solas as High Exorcist. Its Legacy Bourse seat was vacant.
n.Varushka: Varushka held four Senate seats and two generals, with Simargl as Dean of the Lyceum and the Eternal Shafts of Time and Granites of Veltsgorsk in Varushkan hands.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark held three Senate seats and two generals, with Jorma Steelhail as Gatekeeper of Courage, but its Stonefield Ice Caves Bourse seat was recorded as held by the Thule.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: listed with Bohemond de Rondell as its senator.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: listed with Ibrahim, the South Paw, of the Cohort of the Winter Bear as its senator.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: listed with Orrick as senator for the Dour Fens.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: listed with Zephram of Cantiarch's Hold as its senator.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: listed with Oria as its senator.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: listed with Hengest Dun as its senator.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: listed with Ranulf Pridestalker as its senator.
t.Holberg: Holberg's senator was Stern, and the Great Pits of Ennerlund within it were under repair and expected to produce mithril shortly after the solstice.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: listed with Maher i Zaydan i Riqueza as its senator.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: listed with Olle Markusson as its senator.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: listed with Irena Arkady as its senator.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: listed with Maarit as its senator.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: listed with Anwar i Del-Toro i Riquezza as its senator.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: listed with Llewellyn Leafstalker as its senator.
t.Miekarova: Miekarova's senator Dušan Otecovna Zlata had been revoked by the Synod and then re-elected, and could not be revoked again until the seat's next normal election.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: listed with Bridget Eastville as senator for the Pride of the Marches.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: listed with Ariadne as its senator.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: listed with Ianthe of Raven's Watch as its senator.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: listed with Probus of Shattered Spire as its senator.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: listed with Balthasar of the Suns of Couros as senator, and with Azazel of Ravensfell holding the Great Forest at Reikos.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: listed with Alessandra Serafini as its senator.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: listed with Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra as its senator.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: listed with Escalade Carsenere as its senator.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: listed with Atte as its senator.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: listed with Irontide Vio as its senator.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Tanwyn Ankarien was listed as senator for Spiral among the senators of Urizen, and Damian as Castellan of Spiral Castle.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: listed with Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato as its senator.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: listed with Gant Archama as its senator.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: listed with Caerwyn Summer Crow as its senator.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: listed with Silas as senator for the Silver Chase.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: listed with Juha the Cave Spider as its senator.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: listed with Valentin Ivarovich Orzel as senator, and with Soren il Signo holding the Weirwater Vales.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: listed with Edmundo of Endsmeet as its senator.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: The Great Pits of Ennerlund had no holder and were being repaired, with their first load of mithril expected shortly after the Summer Solstice 380YE.

Assign Spiral.d: The motion, proposed by Morrow and seconded by Mitwold, sought to assign Spiral to an Imperial nation. The Senate assigned the territory to Urizen. As a result, Spiral became a Urizen territory and elected its own Senator, gaining representation in the Senate.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page. Spiral, listed as held by Grendel that season, was assigned to Urizen.
n.Urizen: Urizen gained Spiral as one of its territories and with it a new Senator in the Imperial Senate.

t.Spiral: Spiral was formally assigned to the nation of Urizen and elected a Senator to represent it.

Blackest night.d: Scholars at Iteri's Observatory of the Blazing Mirror built a device with Camillius of Endsmeet to study the star. Rumour says their spire fell and its magicians died. The star is visible only in parts of the north, which suggests powerful magic. Its impact would devastate the region it struck, and every resource in Miekarova improved beyond level one would lose a level. Day and Night magic might divine where it will fall, and Autumn magic might shift its path, but no Imperial ritual exists and any working would need to be done in Miekarova or at the Anvil regio. The empty skies spread to Necropolis, Bregasland and Segura. By the resolution the star had grown further, but the Phoenix was plainly visible again.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the red star could be seen over Wickmoor and Sandling in Weirwater.
n.Highguard: The empty-sky phenomenon spread over Necropolis, leaving only the moon and clouds visible at night and unsettling those who studied it.
n.Imperial Orcs: The skies over Skarsind stayed empty of stars except for the crimson star, and naga who spent long periods there found their secretive urges greatly strengthened.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the red star could be seen in the northern sky over Hercynia.
n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast astronomancers were among the first to report the new star, and the empty skies spread over Segura.
n.The League: Holberg remained under the empty, starless skies, and naga who spent long periods beneath the city's inky black sky found it hard to speak openly about their intentions.
n.The Marches: The empty-sky phenomenon spread to Bregasland, leaving its night skies bare of stars.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the star appeared to hover above the mountains separating the northern Empire from the lands of the Thule.
n.Urizen: Scholars of the Observatory of the Blazing Mirror in Iteri tried to study the star closely, and rumour says their spire fell and all its magicians died as a result.
n.Varushka: The star was visible over all of Varushka, and divinations warned that it would strike Miekarova, with devastating loss of life and resources if it hit an important region.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the red star was visible over Sermersuaq and over Northspires and Bruckland in Hahnmark.

t.Bregasland: The empty skies spread to Bregasland, so that by night nothing but the moon and clouds could be seen.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the red star could be seen low in the northern sky over Northspires and Bruckland.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: the red star was visible in the northern sky over Hercynia.
t.Holberg: Holberg's night skies stayed empty of stars, and naga who lingered there found their secretiveness markedly intensified.
t.Karsk: A Karsk cabal tracked the star's approach and foresaw its fall in Miekarova, but its elders chose to leave the problem to the cabals of Miekarova.
t.Miekarova: Divinations pointed to Miekarova as where the star would fall: one region would be utterly devastated, and every resource improved beyond level one would permanently lose a level. Any ritual to divert it would have to be performed there or at the Anvil.
t.Necropolis: The empty-sky phenomenon spread over Necropolis, leaving its nights starless and unsettling to those who studied them.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the page refers only to the mountains that separate the northern Empire from the lands of the Thule.
t.Segura: The starless empty skies spread over Segura, and naga who spent long there found their urge towards secrecy greatly strengthened.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the red star was visible in the northern sky over Sermersuaq.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind's night sky remained empty of stars, yet the crimson star was clearly visible there, the only thing besides the moon that could be seen.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: the red star could be seen over Wickmoor and Sandling.
t.Zenith: The Observatory of the Blazing Mirror in Iteri attempted to study the star, and rumours say its spire fell and its magicians perished.

r.Hahnmark/Bruckland: Mentioned in passing: the red star was visible in the night sky over Bruckland.
r.Hahnmark/Northspires: Mentioned in passing: the red star was visible in the night sky over Northspires.
r.Karsk/Moresvah: A cabal charged with the vales of Moresvah confirmed through observation and Night magic that the star would fall in Miekarova, but its elders decided it was not their concern.
r.Weirwater/Sandling: Mentioned in passing: the red star could be seen over Sandling.
r.Weirwater/Wickmoor: Mentioned in passing: the red star could be seen over Wickmoor.
r.Zenith/Iteri: Iteri's Observatory of the Blazing Mirror built a device to view the star, and its spire is rumoured to have fallen, with all its magicians dead.

Construct Axos Embassy.d: Proposed by Zenith and seconded by Sarvos, the self-funded motion called for an Embassy to Axos in Redoubt. It required 25 wains of weirwood, 25 wains of white granite and 12 thrones in labour, with three months to build and an upkeep of 5 thrones per season from the Senate's budget. After the Summer Solstice, Tanwyn Ankarien supplied all the materials and labour, and construction began in Limus, Cargo, Redoubt, near the Jarmish embassy. Once complete, the embassy will create a new Imperial title, Ambassador to Axos, appointed by the Senate.

n.Urizen: Urizen's Senate seats proposed and seconded the motion through Zenith and Sarvos. The Empire's new diplomatic link with Axos is being built on Urizeni soil in Redoubt.

t.Redoubt: Redoubt will host the Empire's embassy to Axos once the three months of building are finished, adding to the diplomatic presence already there near the Jarmish embassy.

r.Redoubt/Limus: Construction of the Axos embassy began in Cargo, Limus, near the existing Jarmish embassy, after Tanwyn Ankarien supplied the materials and labour.

Construct Cathedral of Courage.d: Proposed by the senator for Weirwater and seconded by Semmerholm, the motion called for a cathedral dedicated to Courage in Astolat as a sinecure providing Synod votes, with its Dean to be chosen by the National Assembly of Dawn. It passed at a cost of 25 thrones, which were disbursed to Senator Weirwater. Valentin Ivarovich Severyan contributed 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns after the Summer Solstice. Because some necessary details were missing from the motion, Senator Weirwater was left to decide them. The result was a small cathedral close to the tourney grounds of Laroc in The Chase, overseen by the Dean of Laroc Cathedral.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish gained a cathedral meant to strengthen their Courage against malign influences, with its Dean, the Dean of Laroc Cathedral, chosen by the National Assembly of Dawn and holding Synod votes.

t.Astolat: Astolat became home to a new small cathedral to Courage, raised with Senate funding and donated white granite.

r.Astolat/The Chase: The new Cathedral of Courage stands in The Chase, close to the tourney grounds of Laroc.

Construct Gardens of High Chalcis.d: Using construction powers delegated by the Senate, the Highguard Civilian Commissioner approved this great work to seize an opportunity that arose after Reikos was reclaimed. It cost 80 wains of weirwood and six months to build, all supplied by Rhesa in two instalments with 160 crowns in total. Once finished, the gardens yield 120 herbs each season, shared among Reikos citizens who own herb gardens, and increase the prosperity of Reikos. The motion also proposed a ceremonial title, Master Botanist of High Chalcis, appointed by the Highguard Senators. After extensive constitutional scrutiny this was found to exceed a Civilian Commissioner's powers, so the title was not created and responsibility falls to the Senator for Reikos.

n.Highguard: Highguard's Civilian Commissioner and Exarch Rhesa commissioned and personally funded the gardens. However, the proposed title to be appointed by the Highguard Senators was ruled beyond the Commissioner's power and was not created.

t.Reikos: Reikos gained a great work that increases its prosperity and provides 120 herbs each season to its citizens who own herb gardens. Its Senator holds responsibility for any threats or decisions concerning the gardens.

r.Reikos/Chalcis Mount: The Gardens of High Chalcis were rebuilt in Chalcis Mount, with work finished shortly before the Winter Solstice 380YE.

Construct Gardens of Morrow.d: Acting under the power to commission constructions delegated by the Senate, the Civilian Commissioner of Urizen approved the Gardens of Morrow as a great work in Morrow. It cost 40 wains of weirwood and 10 thrones in labour, and took three months to build. The materials and money were provided by Juliana after the Spring Equinox 381YE. Once complete, the Gardens of Morrow provide 75 herbs, split equally among the citizens who own herb gardens in Morrow.

n.Urizen: Urizen's own Civilian Commissioner approved the great work, and once complete it yields herbs to Urizeni citizens who own herb gardens in Morrow.

t.Morrow: Morrow gains the Gardens of Morrow, a great work that provides 75 herbs, shared equally among the territory's herb garden owners.

Construct General Estana's Repository.d: The motion proposed building a grand library of contracts in the town of Oran, costing one wain of white granite, 2 crowns in labour and three months to construct. It would be dedicated to the Eternal Callidus, whose heralds would in return help the Hakima codify Autumn rituals. The motion sought permission to build in advance, with construction to start only once a contract with Callidus or one of his heralds was signed. Concerns were noted because a Civilian Commissioner cannot commission anything requiring upkeep. If the project seemed to create something with an upkeep, work would stop and the Senate would be consulted. With no contract signed, nothing was built and the commission lapsed.

n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast's Civilian Commissioner approved the folly in return for Callidus's heralds helping the Hakima codify Autumn rituals. Because no contract with the Eternal was signed, the nation gained neither the library nor that assistance.

t.Feroz: The town of Oran in Feroz was chosen as the site for General Estana's Repository, but no construction took place there and the commission lapsed.

Construct Reinos Spy Network.d: The motion, proposed by Madruga and seconded by Therunin, sought Senate approval to build a spy network in the Lasambrian Hills of Reinos, at that time held by the Jotun. The motion failed, so no spy network was commissioned there as a result of this proposal. The page records no vote tallies or further consequences.

n.Jotun: The Jotun held Reinos at the time, and the failed motion meant the Empire did not commission a spy network to watch the lands they occupied.

t.Reinos: A proposed spy network in Reinos's Lasambrian Hills, then under Jotun control, was not built after the Senate motion failed.

Construct Sarcophan Delves Embassy.d: The motion passed at a cost of 200 thrones, which were disbursed to Senator Mitwold. Construction also needed 25 wains of weirwood, 25 wains of white granite and 12 thrones in labour, and took three months. Thanmir Hrafnar supplied all of these materials and labour costs. The motion did not say where the embassy should stand, so the senator for Mitwold chose the City of Cargo in Redoubt. Completing the embassy automatically created a new Imperial title, Ambassador to the Sarcophan Delves. Its upkeep is 5 thrones per season, paid from the Senate's budget.

n.Urizen: The Empire's new embassy to the Sarcophan Delves stands in the Urizen-held territory of Redoubt, which gives the nation a hosting role in the Empire's formal relations with the Sarcophan Delves.

t.Redoubt: The completed embassy was built in the City of Cargo in Redoubt, where the senator for Mitwold chose to site it.

Construct Trading Post of Karov.d: The motion commissioned a trading post in Karov, approved by the Civilian Commissioner of Varushka under the Senate's delegated power to commission constructions. Its stated purpose was to seize an opportunity to improve the wealth of Skarsind. The work cost 8 wains of white granite and 2 thrones in labour, and was to take three months to build. Nadezhda Nadyovna Gremani provided the full materials and funding after the Summer Solstice 380YE. On completion, the project created the title of Overseer of the Westward Road, a national Imperial title.

n.Imperial Orcs: The trading post was commissioned to improve the wealth of Skarsind, an Imperial Orc territory, which made the Orcs among the intended beneficiaries.
n.Varushka: Varushka's Civilian Commissioner approved the trading post on Varushkan land in Karov, and Nadezhda Nadyovna Gremani supplied the granite and thrones needed to build it.

t.Karov: Karov became the site of the new trading post, built with 8 wains of white granite and 2 thrones over three months. On completion it created the title of Overseer of the Westward Road.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind was the territory whose wealth the trading post was meant to improve, according to the motion's stated purpose.

Construct Valley of Pride.d: The commission was approved by the Civilian Commissioner of Wintermark, using the power to commission constructions that the Senate had delegated to them. The Valley of Pride is a sinecure costing twelve wains of weirwood and three thrones in labour, and takes three months to build. Thanmir Hrafnar provided the weirwood and the thrones after the Summer Solstice 380YE. Once completed, the sinecure will create the Wintermark national title of Herbalist of the Hearth. The holder is to be appointed by unanimous decision of the Wintermark senators.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gains a new national title, the Herbalist of the Hearth, chosen by unanimous decision of its senators, with Thanmir Hrafnar meeting the full cost of materials and labour.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark is to gain a herb sinecure, the Valley of Pride, built within its borders on Wintermark land.

r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: Wood Heath is the chosen site of the Valley of Pride, a herb sinecure taking three months to build.

Construct statue of Janon.d: Using the power to commission constructions delegated by the Senate, the Civilian Commissioner of the League approved a statue of the Eternal Janon in Hanuri in Temeschwar, with no Imperial title attached. It cost one wain of white granite and two crowns in labour, and took three months to build. Drogon Morosini provided the granite and the crowns after the Summer Solstice 380YE. The folly did not last: shortly before the Spring Equinox 383YE the statue was reduced to expensive rubble.

n.The League: The League's Civilian Commissioner approved this folly to Janon on League soil, and a League citizen, Drogon Morosini, paid for its construction.

t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar gained a white granite statue of the Eternal Janon, which was later reduced to rubble shortly before the Spring Equinox 383YE.

r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: Hanuri was the site of the statue of Janon, built from 380YE and destroyed shortly before the Spring Equinox 383YE.

Construct the Dour Fens.d: The Civilian Commissioner of the Marches commissioned the Dour Fens, a mana sinecure in Graven, Bregasland, using the power to commission constructions that the Senate had delegated to them. The exact cost was not recorded, though standard costs applied. After the Winter Solstice of 380YE, Silas Merrick provided 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns towards the work. Once completed, the sinecure will create the Marcher national title of Keeper of the Dour Fens. It is a lifetime appointment made by the Marcher Senators, who must agree unanimously.

n.The Marches: The Marches gain a new national position, the Keeper of the Dour Fens. The Marcher Senators will appoint the holder for life by unanimous decision once the sinecure is complete.

t.Bregasland: The Dour Fens mana sinecure is to be built in Graven, Bregasland, and Silas Merrick provided mithril and crowns towards its construction after Winter Solstice 380YE.

Construct the Skarsind School of Warcast.d: The commission called for a mana sinecure in Estermark, Skarsind, at standard but unrecorded cost. Bloodcrow Yargol supplied 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns after the Summer Solstice 380YE. Once complete, the sinecure is to create a national title for the Skarsind College of Warcasting. The motion text names it Headteacher, a lifetime appointment by the Imperial Orcs Senators. The campaign outcome names it Preceptor, appointed by unanimous decision of the Imperial Orcs Senators. The page does not record the project as completed.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs' Civilian Commissioner approved the commission. Once complete, it will give the nation a new national title over the Skarsind College of Warcasting, appointed by the Imperial Orcs Senators.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind, held by the Imperial Orcs, is to host a new mana sinecure, with mithril and crowns already supplied towards its construction.

r.Skarsind/Estermark: Estermark is the chosen site for the Skarsind School of Warcasting, a mana sinecure commissioned in Summer 380YE.

Declare peace with Orcs of the Great For.d: The motion extended all the legal protections and responsibilities of foreigners to the orcs of the Great Forest of Peytaht. It followed two earlier motions concerning the orcs of the Barrens: the first declared peace, and the second declared war on the orcs of that territory collectively. As a result of this declaration, the orcs of the Great Forest of Peytaht were recognised as foreigners under Imperial law. This distinguished them in law from the other orcs of the Barrens.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the motion concerns the orcs of the Barrens, and the Druj are not named in it, though the earlier declaration of war against the collective orcs of that territory forms the background.

t.The Barrens: The motion carved the orcs of the Great Forest of Peytaht out from the collective declaration of war on the orcs of the Barrens, giving them the protections of foreigners under Imperial law.

Disburse funds for Iron Helms III.d: The motion sought Senate funds to finish raising the Iron Helms army, which the Senate had commissioned in Autumn 379YE. It was the third such funding motion, following two earlier ones. Proposed by the senator for Karsk and seconded by Hahnmark, it passed in principle and was approved at 200 thrones. The 200 thrones were then disbursed to the senator for Karsk to put towards the army's completion.

n.Varushka: Varushka moved closer to fielding a new army, the Iron Helms, as 200 thrones went to its senator for Karsk to help complete it.

t.Karsk: The Iron Helms army was being raised in Karsk, and the territory's senator proposed the motion and received the 200 thrones disbursed to complete it.

Enlargement of The Black Thorns.d: Proposed by Therunin and seconded by Karsk, the motion passed in principle and was approved at 200 thrones, which were disbursed to Senator Therunin. The work required 100 wains of mithril, 25 thrones in labour costs and six months to complete, and raised the army's upkeep to 75 thrones per season. The materials were supplied by Caerwyn in two instalments: 50 wains of mithril and 15 thrones after the Summer Solstice 380YE, and a further 50 wains of mithril and 10 thrones after the Autumn Equinox 380YE.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; the motion refers only to the retaking of Liathaven, a territory then in Jotun hands.

t.Liathaven: The campaign to retake Liathaven from its Jotun holders provided the opportunity that the motion used to justify expanding the Black Thorns into a large army.

O rose thou art sick.d: Despite rumours that many de Lusignan nobles had taken their own lives, curses continued. In Astolat, Dawn's witches identified a curse, almost certainly Night magic, that inflamed noble rivalries and stirred yeofolk resentment, especially around Laroc. Astolat soldiers questioned orders and some deserted. Their warbands lost a quarter of their fighting strength unless doing paid work. Tassato suffered stinking heat from Icy Maw Devours the Spark of Essence, which halved its crystalline mana. Naeve's Twisting Blight halved Casinea's farm production. These curses ran their course by the Summer Solstice. The Winter curse on the Court of the White Fountain persisted, slowed but not reversed by the Spire of the Auric Horizon's magic.

n.Dawn: Astolat's nobles saw tempers flare into Tests of Resolve, yeofolk grew insolent and questioned old traditions, and Astolat soldiers wherever they served became slow to obey, with some desertions.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: an Astolat seneschal fumes that the abandoned keep could have been attacked by Druj.
n.Highguard: Highborn farms in Casinea were devastated by three rainless months, with crop failures, food poisoning and a few deaths before the blight passed.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: fear of the Jotun after their conquest of the Mournwold left Tassato's discontented citizens subdued.
n.The League: Tassato's people endured a stinking, oppressive heat, and its magicians suffered malaise while the city's mana sources yielded only half their usual crystal mana.
n.Urizen: The Court of the White Fountain in Redoubt continued to crumble under a Winter curse, and the Spire of the Auric Horizon's magic delayed but did not reverse the decline.

t.Astolat: A curse spread from the eastern woodlands, setting yeofolk against nobles, prompting talk near Laroc of whether their ancestors should have marched west, and undermining discipline among local soldiers.
t.Casinea: No rain fell from the Spring Equinox to the Summer Solstice, halving all farm production. Spoiled food and hidden thirst caused some deaths before the curse abated.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun conquest of the Mournwold weighed on the minds of Tassato's people.
t.Redoubt: The fortification at Optarion was still being eroded by a Winter curse, held back only by the Auric Horizon's adamant and Summer magic.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: wags noted that people had also called Sarvos too damp to burn.
t.Tassato: An unseasonable heatwave festered the spring floodwaters into a great stink, weak regio collapsed and mana sources produced only half their normal output until the Solstice.

r.Redoubt/Optarion: The Court of the White Fountain's plume of fire guttered and its white stone cracked again, and the decline was slowed but not reversed.

Raise Wintermark army II.d: The motion permitted the Winterfolk to begin raising a new army at a cost of 200 wains of mithril and 50 thrones, taking a year to raise and requiring upkeep of 50 thrones a season from the Senate's budget. Scrutiny required the proposing senator to name the Wintermark region where the army would be raised. Hengest Dun supplied the materials in instalments between the Winter Solstice 381YE and the Winter Solstice 382YE, completing the 200 wains of mithril and 50 thrones. The new army was to muster in Kallavesa, and on completion a new national title of general would be created.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gained the prospect of an additional army and a new national general's title, with the mithril and thrones to build it provided over several seasons by Hengest Dun.

t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa was named as the territory where the new Wintermark army would muster.

Raise a glass.d: Citizens across the Empire, especially in Holberg, Tassato and Temeschwar, prepared bunting, commemorative plates and food for week-long street parties. Private donations covered only minor festivities. A Senate motion could appoint someone to organise the celebrations, release Imperial funds and receive donations and Virtue fund allocations. There were three tiers: grand celebrations at 80 thrones, breath-taking at 250 and wondrous at 500. Larger celebrations would bring a greater surge in morale and Virtue, shaped by the Throne's message. Past Thrones such as Britta, James, Nicovar and Teleri had used their messages to secure lasting benefits. The Senate disbursed 40 thrones and appointed Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato to oversee the preparations.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: a grand tourney for Dawnish citizens was described as part of the possible 500-throne wondrous celebrations.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj-held Barrens appear only in a historical example, the repair of the Tower of the Dawn funded by donations after Emperor James's coronation.
n.The League: The new Empress was one of the League's own, and its cities led the preparations. Proud League citizens were urged to dig deep to celebrate her elevation, and its cities would become wonderlands if the most lavish celebrations were funded.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: magical light displays imported from Urizen, and glass bridges linking its spires, were described as features of the larger possible celebrations.

t.Holberg: Holberg was one of the League territories abuzz with preparations for the festivities that would follow the coronation.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos, still wounded from its occupation, had weathered the storm and was eagerly looking forward to the coronation.
t.Tassato: Tassato was busy preparing for the coronation festivities. Its senator, Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato, was appointed by the Senate to oversee the celebrations.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar was among the League territories most caught up in preparations for the festivities, and some citizens believed the new Empress was Temeschwari.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens were cited as the site of the Tower of the Dawn, whose repair was largely funded by donations after Emperor James's coronation.

Rebirth in Reikos.d: After more than a decade of deliberate Druj ruin, Reikos was transformed after the Spring Equinox: fungi and moulds sprang up everywhere, poisoned waters ran clean, and ruins were overgrown. Yael and Jared, backed by Synod judgements and a large bounty of liao, countered the heretic Golan's message of Courage as the prime virtue. Many of Golan's followers returned to their congregations, while others joined the new Congregation of the First Empress. Some called the change a miracle of a living paragon; others blamed fell Realm creatures, noting memorials drowned beneath the growth. The Synod could boost, spread or counter the movement. In the event, it supported Jared, Cardinal of Loyalty, in spreading Yael's teachings across the entire Empire.

n.Druj: The lingering legacy of the Druj occupation, including the poisoned wells and fouled streams they left behind, was being washed away by the new growth sweeping Reikos.
n.Highguard: The Highborn people of Reikos, broken by Druj oppression, turned from Golan's heresy to Yael's message, with many rejoining their old congregations and others swelling the fervent Congregation of the First Empress, a movement the Synod then chose to spread across the Empire.

t.Reikos: Reikos was physically and spiritually reborn as fungi and greenery overran the ruins and cleansed poisoned waters, while Yael and Jared's preaching birthed the Congregation of the First Empress there, though some memorials and graves were drowned beneath the growth.

Small things and large.d: The Spring planting in Bregasland, Upwold and Mitwold was ruined by torrential rain and Naeve's Twisting Blight, which had faded by the Summer solstice. Catastrophic news from the Mourn followed. Rather than turning on each other, Marchers helped their neighbours, though they treated that aid as a loan. Meade's alders, knowing the towns starve when the farmers do, proposed granaries and seed stores, and alders across the Marches contributed funds. The work needed 100 wains of weirwood, 40 wains of white granite and 35 Thrones, and would take two seasons. It promised to boost farm income in each territory and to halve army decay for one struggling nation. The Senate commissioned it, with completion expected by Spring Equinox 381YE. Decisions on it later passed to the Keeper of the Breadbasket in autumn 381YE.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun-held Mournwold is referred to only through the catastrophic news from the Mourn and the Marchers' sacrifices to free it.
n.The Marches: Marcher farms suffered a second ruined crop, but the market towns and alders pulled together to fund a granary network. It was meant to support every Marcher farm and to help mend the rift between town and country.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland's Spring planting was blighted, and it was one of the three territories to receive the new granaries and seed stores, with the extra income they were expected to bring its farms.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold's farms lost their Spring planting to rain and blight. Meade, which relies on Mitwold's produce, launched the granary plan that would extend into the territory.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the page refers to catastrophic news from the Mourn, and to Marcher farmers selling their food so the armies could try to free the Mournwold.
t.Upwold: Upwold's crops were again ruined by the curse, and the territory was included in the granary and seed-store network the Senate commissioned.

Sorrow and death.d: During the Spring Equinox a riot engulfed the Spire, which treated those broken by dangerous magic, and several dangerous patients escaped. Its last Arbiter, Papiria, murdered a healer and vanished. Nazares, a former warmage obsessed with destroying the Druj, raised the dead as husks, attacked spires in eastern Lustri and marched north towards Embersfall Spire. A subtle Winter pall of sadness, blamed on three women who became vessels of the Three Sisters, spread through Proceris and Occursion. The Conclave was offered the chance to name a group to succeed the Spire, with a Custodian of the Lost. At the Solstice the husks collapsed, and Urizen priests freed the pall's source.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the unliving horde marching through Dawn-held Weirwater is cited as a far larger threat than Nazares' husks.
n.Druj: Nazares sought to raise an army for an insane war to "extinguish the foul Druj" and may have been heading for the Mallum border, while the pall of sorrow was seen as a weakness the Druj would be quick to exploit.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Zenith's shared border with the Grendel is noted as one of the real dangers its people blamed for their grim mood.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the strengthening pall was likened to the miasma that until recently smothered Highguard-held Reikos.
n.Urizen: Urizen lost the Spire of Twisting Shadows, saw outlying spires attacked by husks and its people weighed down by a curse of sorrow, but the husks collapsed and Urizen priests lifted the pall at the Cave of the Weeping Sisters.

t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the miasma that until recently smothered Reikos is used as a comparison for how the pall of sorrow might worsen.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: the unliving threat marching through Weirwater is described as far larger than Nazares' corpse-herd.
t.Zenith: Zenith faced two magical threats at once, a growing husk-legion picking off isolated spires and a creeping Winter pall that threatened to sap its people's will and output, until both ended by the Summer Solstice.

r.Zenith/Lustri: The Spire of Twisting Shadows in Lustri's forest foothills was lost to riot, Nazares' husks attacked spires in eastern Lustri and moved north towards Embersfall Spire, and the pall of sorrow began here.
r.Zenith/Occursion: The pall spread into Occursion, and it was at the Cave of the Weeping Sisters here that Urizen priests persuaded a magician trapped between life and death to move on, breaking the Three Sisters' hold.
r.Zenith/Proceris: The pall of sorrow spread through Proceris over the three months before the Summer Solstice, bringing sadness, regret and visions of two figures weeping over a third.

Spreading the word.d: Since the death of Empress Britta, Livia Cascade's Torchbearers had been recording citizens' accounts of Past-Life Visions. The Spider's Vantage Spire in Redoubt then published them Empire-wide. Citizens across the Empire devoured them eagerly. Navarri shuddered at a remembered fall of Terunael, Highborn debated an ancient exarch honouring a herald, Winterfolk scops retold their last King's negotiations with the First Empress' ambassador, and some Imperial Orc preachers bristled at mentions of their enslaved ancestors. Storytellers from less austere traditions embellished the tales freely. The accounts are retellings of other people's stories, not guaranteed to be true, and their widespread publication is expected to have unpredictable effects in years to come.

n.Urizen: Urizen's Torchbearers, led by Livia Cascade, the Seer of the Gateway, compiled the accounts, and a Redoubt publishing-house spread them across the Empire, making Urizen the source of the first published Past-Life Visions in living memory.

t.Redoubt: The Spider's Vantage Spire, a publishing-house in Redoubt, printed the accounts and distributed them throughout the Empire.

Statement of Intent regarding the Stalke.d: The Stalker, a red star then believed to be set to fall in Miekarova, prompted this motion. Proposed by the senator for Volodmartz and seconded by the senator for Hercynia, it framed the diversion as part of the Empire's ongoing peace treaty with the Thule and as acceptance of a Thule gesture of goodwill. The Senate agreed in principle that the Thule ritual should be used to redirect the comet away from Imperial land and onto Sküld, a Thule territory. The motion was a statement of intent that passed in principle; the page does not record whether the ritual was carried out.

n.Thule: The Thule offered the ritual as a gesture of goodwill under the peace treaty, and the Senate agreed in principle to have the Stalker diverted onto their own territory of Sküld.
n.Varushka: The motion sought to spare Varushka's territory of Miekarova from the red star, and it was proposed by the senator for Volodmartz, a Varushkan territory.

t.Miekarova: Miekarova was where the Stalker was believed to be set to fall, and the motion aimed to divert the comet away from it.

Temple of the bull.d: The Asaveans shipped about fifty wains of white granite to Oran under warship escort, brought no slaves and paid Imperial labourers handsomely. Once complete, the temple was expected to warm relations with the Archipelago, improve business income across Feroz and create an Asavean-appointed liaison chosen with guidance from Feroz's senator. Asavea also invited the Way to build a temple in Nemoria. The Assembly of Nine judged that assisting construction was idolatry, and Abaddon de Rondell's work in Feroz slowed the project and raised its labour costs, likely creating a diplomatic incident. Jorma Steelhail's call to destroy the temple failed 327 to 421; a motion funding the Nemoria temple was withdrawn after a theft.

n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn faced a foreign temple to Asavean idols rising in Oran, with even their relaxed priests resenting it, while Freeborn labourers were offered lucrative work that the Synod now declared idolatrous. Senator Pedro i Taziel i Riquezz was invited to put forward candidates for liaison with the Asavean priests.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the completed temple was expected to draw traders away from other ports around the Bay of Catazar.
t.Feroz: Feroz hosted the Asavean temple and stood to gain a modest boost to business income from traders it attracted, but Abaddon de Rondell's preaching against it pushed completion back to shortly before the Spring Equinox 381YE.

r.Feroz/Oranseri: The temple was being built at the port of Oran, where Asavean warships had escorted the granite cargo and where the Synod's named priest worked to discourage local labourers from joining the project.

The other empress.d: During the occupation of Sarvos, Highborn Unconquered seized Giselle's coffin before the Grendel could defile it. With help from League heroes they escaped through the Sentinel Gate to Anvil. Magistrates impounded the coffin near Sybella because Giselle's reported wish to be buried in the League had never been written down or witnessed. Highborn Stewards of the Dead argued for the traditional burial in the Necropolis, while League bishops called moving her an attack on League Pride. The Senate was asked to choose a site and commission a tomb with an Imperial title, but passed no motion. Her husband Teodore's body had been stolen by the Grendel. Virtue's Respite in Temeschwar was completed shortly before Spring 381YE.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the in-character vignette shows two Dawnish folk, a retired Weirwater advocate and a Hawsmoor pig farmer, discussing a wager on where Giselle will be buried.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the in-character text recalls that Giselle died in agony from Druj poison, which casts doubt on her deathbed wishes.
n.Grendel: Grendel raiders broke open Giselle's tomb in Sarvos and took its grave goods, though the Unconquered had already removed her coffin. They also tore apart her husband Teodore's sarcophagus and carried off his body, for reasons no one knows.
n.Highguard: Highborn Unconquered saved the Empress's remains, and Highborn Stewards of the Dead argued that only the Necropolis could protect her and uphold tradition. In the end she was re-interred in the League, not Highguard.
n.The League: League heroes helped the Unconquered escape with the coffin, and League bishops condemned any move to bury Giselle outside the League as an attack on its Pride. Her eventual re-interment in Temeschwar respected her reported wish to rest in the League.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Wintermark Empresses Mariika and Britta are cited as precedents for Thrones who were not entombed in the Necropolis.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Marcher abbots wrote urging the Senators of Highguard and the League to fortify the Bay of Catazar coast against further Grendel raids.
t.Casinea: Magistrates intercepted the Unconquered just outside Sybella, impounded Giselle's coffin and held it in a cellar there while the Senate considered the matter.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Giselle reportedly refused burial in the Necropolis during the retreat from Holberg.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: Empress Britta, whose burial was similarly disputed, was given to the marshes of Kallavesa as a precedent.
t.Necropolis: The Necropolis, traditional resting place of almost every Throne, was proposed for Giselle's new tomb on the grounds that it could be properly protected. It was not chosen.
t.Sarvos: Giselle's marble tomb on the Alivetti estates in Sarvos was effectively destroyed by the Grendel. Highborn critics argued that Sarvos could not protect a new tomb against further raids.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the territory is touched on only through the Wintermark precedents for Thrones not laid in the Necropolis.
t.Temeschwar: Bishop Jago Heshel di Temeschwar led the League bishops who opposed moving Giselle out of the League. Shortly before Spring 381YE she was re-interred in Temeschwar, in the new tomb of Virtue's Respite.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Isolde, who appears in the in-character vignette, was once the best advocate in Weirwater.

The prime colour of the world.d: The Hallow was the first such Empire-wide enchantment since before Emperor Hugh's reign. Every herb garden produced extra Cerulean Mazzarine, and animals, plants and people grew more fertile. Briars felt their lineage strengthened, and weak Spring regio and heralds stirred. Floodwaters spread a Rivers of Life curse along the Scorrero, boosting farms and gardens in Kahraman, Segura and Madruga. Realmsroot bloomed in Upwold, Hahnmark and Miaren. Dawn's new Gardens of Tiberius' Bequest were offered a mithril upgrade, which was never taken. In Holberg, Rebeshof became marsh, cutting farm production. Ennerlund was threatened next, with options to save it or embrace the marsh, but no immediate effort was made.

n.Dawn: The newly built Gardens of Tiberius' Bequest in Laroc were found to sit on a Spring regio, offering a chance to boost production with mithril mirrors, but the opportunity was not taken and lapsed.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are noted as having destroyed paths and bridges in Holberg that any new dike-building would try to replace.
n.Navarr: Navarr's trods pulsed with Spring magic but needed far more clearing, and Realmsroot bloomed in unprecedented quantities in Miaren.
n.The Brass Coast: The Hallow amplified the Rivers of Life curse carried down the Scorrero by floodwaters, further enhancing every farm and herb garden in Kahraman, Segura and Madruga.
n.The League: The enchantment worsened the Morass in Holberg, turning Rebeshof to marsh and cutting the territory's farm production, with Ennerlund threatened next and costly options offered to save it or turn it into a herb-rich marsh.
n.The Marches: Realmsroot, a rare herb with a powerful narcotic effect on the lineaged, bloomed in unprecedented quantities across Upwold.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Sherard Hunters wove the Hallow of the Green World, and Realmsroot bloomed in unprecedented quantities in Hahnmark.

t.Astolat: The Gardens of Tiberius' Bequest in Laroc could have been made more fertile by harnessing a Spring regio at their centre, but the opportunity was not taken.
t.Hahnmark: Rare Realmsroot bloomed in unprecedented quantities across Hahnmark, and herb gardens there yielded prepared doses of it.
t.Holberg: The Hallow accelerated the Morass, making Rebeshof a marsh and permanently reducing farm production, while Ennerlund faced the same fate by Winter unless 60 wains of weirwood and 15 Thrones were spent.
t.Kahraman: The Rivers of Life evoked in Kahraman was made especially potent, further boosting every farm and herb garden in the territory.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: its marshes are the benchmark for healing herbs that a deliberately tended Holberg marsh might nearly rival.
t.Madruga: Floodwaters along the Scorrero carried the empowered Rivers of Life downstream, enhancing every farm and herb garden in Madruga.
t.Miaren: Rare Realmsroot bloomed in unprecedented quantities across Miaren, and herb gardens there yielded prepared doses of it.
t.Segura: The empowered Rivers of Life, spread by floodwaters down the Scorrero, further enhanced every farm and herb garden in Segura.
t.Upwold: Rare Realmsroot bloomed in unprecedented quantities across Upwold, and herb gardens there yielded prepared doses of it.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Ennerlund was set to become a marsh by the Winter Solstice, sooner if further strong Spring magic struck, which would raise the upkeep of the Great Pits of Ennerlund; the Senate could pay to save it or to turn it into a tended herb marsh.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: Without dike repairs, large parts of Rebeshof reverted to sodden marsh and the region was officially declared a marsh, too late to prevent.
r.Holberg/The Morass: The Hallow exacerbated the already worrying spread of the Morass, which swallowed Rebeshof and continued to advance without immediate efforts to contain it.

The twentieth empress.d: Lisabetta, founder of the House of Seven Mirrors and Prince of the Hearthfire Guild of Arms and Artisans, rose swiftly after her first Anvil summit in Winter 378YE, serving as Conscience of the Senate and then as proxy to the Warmage. After nearly a year of campaigning she won the Senate's support. Her coronation was to begin with a procession through the ten nations, ending with her chosen Cardinal crowning her. Asavea, Jarm, the Commonwealth, Faraden, Axos and Sarcophan, along with the Grendel, Jotun and Thule orcs, signalled they would send gifts. Historians wondered whether she would challenge Dawn for the title of monarch.

n.Dawn: Empress Lisabetta might challenge for the title of Monarch of Dawn, though as a League citizen she could not fight in the resulting tourney and would need Dawnish nobles to fight on her behalf; no Throne has sought it since Empress Brannan.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: an in-character civil servant had compared citizens who fail to address the Throne properly to the Druj, a remark that was edited out.
n.Grendel: The Grendel informed the civil service that they intended to send gifts to the new Empress in recognition of her coronation.
n.Jotun: The Jotun informed the civil service that they intended to send gifts to the new Empress in recognition of her coronation.
n.The League: A League citizen, Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, became the twentieth Throne of the Empire, with roots in Tassato, Temeschwar and Holberg.
n.Thule: The Thule informed the civil service that they intended to send gifts to the new Empress in recognition of her coronation.

t.Holberg: The new Empress takes her name from Holberg, where six years earlier she established a new branch of her family's Hearthfire Guild after becoming its Prince.
t.Tassato: The Empress's mother, Elise Giacomi, is of Tassato, and Lisabetta studied music and philosophy at the prestigious University of Tassato.
t.Temeschwar: The Empress's father, Gyorgy Yakovitch, is of Temeschwar, home of her family's long-established Hearthfire Guild of Arms and Artisans.
